startup.name: Minicor
startup.description: Minicor lets AI startups call legacy Windows desktop apps that have no API. A customer describes a workflow and gets an API endpoint; each call runs a self healing automation on a Windows VM, on premises, in the cloud or over Citrix. Observability includes video replay, logging and Slack alerts. Customers are AI companies that need to reach legacy systems on behalf of their own clients.

yc_acceptance.basis: Note only: the company is already accepted to YC Spring 2026, so this is not a forecast. Prior of about 1 percent for a random applicant (yc_acceptance.md) is not informative here. The work is in the ladder.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: Not applicable because the company was accepted. A reviewer would most plausibly worry that computer use agents from model labs and UiPath make a thin wrapper around Windows VMs easy to copy. Because acceptance is already a fact in this test, the estimate is a placeholder and the forecast value sits in the funding ladder that follows.

ladder.why_it_fails: Later rounds fail if growth decays once the early AI customers saturate, or if hyperscalers bundle agent desktops cheaply. Bird style breakout cases are rare and the sample at this stage is small, so the odds are close to the all year base rate with a modest discount.

outcomes.why_it_fails: Most likely a stall or a small acquihire by an RPA or agent platform, since the same capability can be built by a well funded rival within months and VM cost and flakiness cap margins. A meaningful exit needs a durable lead in a category where rivals can copy features and raise more money, and most companies in the reference cohort stay small, are acquired cheaply or stop operating before that point.

killers.risk: Computer use from model labs and UiPath, Microsoft and AWS commoditizes Windows desktop control
killers.evidence: UiPath says its computer use covers desktop and Citrix, and Microsoft and AWS market managed agent desktops for apps without APIs.
killers.mitigation: Win on reliability, self healing and observability for production, and own customer integrations.

killers.risk: Customers are AI startups with small revenue, so demand is concentrated and fragile
killers.evidence: The buyer is other early AI companies, whose own volume determines usage; Skyvern needed years for a seed.
killers.mitigation: Move to direct enterprise and healthcare accounts.

killers.risk: Unit economics: VM, vision model and human repair cost leave thin margins
killers.evidence: Each call runs a Windows VM and a model; Citrix and on premises deployments need onsite work.
killers.mitigation: Cache learned flows, replace vision calls with deterministic steps once stable.

technical_complexity.rationale: A small team can build VM orchestration, vision driven control and replay in three months. Reliability across Citrix, latency and self healing at scale are hard but solvable, and depend on third party vision model quality and speed.

takeover_risk.rationale: Rivals have the distribution and incentive and could ship a comparable endpoint in under a year; the defense is production grade reliability and customer relationships rather than technology.

evidence.claim: UiPath still grows at 13 percent on about 1.6B revenue, showing enterprises pay to automate legacy interfaces.
Hyperscalers are building desktops for agents because many apps have no API.

brand.rationale: An invented short name is a common pattern among YC infrastructure companies and neither helps nor hurts, as with Firecrawl where the product mattered more than the name.

narrative.headline: A real but crowded wedge: seed is likely, later rounds depend on beating computer use from big platforms.
narrative.general_summary: Minicor sells reliable API access to legacy Windows apps for AI startups. Demand is real and the AI infrastructure funding climate is warm, which makes a seed more likely than not. The doubts start at Series A: peers like Cyberdesk and Skyvern show slow funding, and UiPath, Microsoft and model labs can ship the same capability. The story improves if it lands enterprise or healthcare end clients with real volume. The forecast treats the day one description as the best case, anchors on the 2022 to 2024 cohort of researched YC companies, and widens the uncertainty because funding data for recent batches is incomplete and right censored.

assumptions: Pretend date is 2026-04-06 and only the input file describes the company.
Seed means a round above about 500K within about 12 months of batch start.
Base rate cohort B2B 2022 to 2024 has right censoring, so known only rates are biased low.
